source.quote: Audio-gd's own pages for the R-1 MK3, read 2026-11-25 - the product page, its sibling spec file R1mk3EN_Specs.htm and its manual R1mk3EN_Use.htm. « Truly balanced fully discrete r2r ladder DAC »; « 8 group fully discrete R-2R DA converters (2 pcs DA-7 board) implementing balanced mode. »; « 4 fully discrete native DSD decoders work in balanced mode . »; « All inputs with galavanic isolator »; « Built in mulriple OS and NOS modes »; « 5, Real balance DAC design ,built in 4 group fully discrete real balanced DSD native decoders , 8 group fully discrete R-2R PCM decoders and 32bit / PCM384K /DSD512 asynchronous transfer Amanero 384 . »; « 10, DOP support from SPDIF input . »; « 3. Built-in 2X, 4X and 8X digital filters and different NOS modes allow users to choose the tone that best suits their personal taste. » Spec rows: « Support Sampling | USB & IIS : 44.1kHz - 384kHz /32Bit DSD64-512 / Coaxial mode: 44.1, 48, 88.2, 96,192kHz »; « S/N Ratio | >110DB »; « THD+N | <0.01% ». Manual: « "IN1",for the USB digital input. » « "IN2", for the HDMI-IIS digital input; » « "IN3", for the coaxial digital input; » Typos « galavanic » and « mulriple » are the maker's.

facts.chip: « 8 group fully discrete R-2R DA converters (2 pcs DA-7 board) » plus « 4 fully discrete native DSD decoders » - no part number, because the ladder IS the converter. The USB receiver is an « Amanero 384 ».

device_settings.why: The device has a user-selectable non-oversampling mode, set from the front panel or the remote. The maker's own mode list, from the user manual: « The 2nd and 3rd digit from the left on bottom: OS and NOS mode select. While working under oversampling (OS) mode, the lower the oversampling level is, the warmer the sound will be. While working under non-oversampling (NOS) mode , the sound even more warmer and smoother. The possible values are: N0 : New NOS mode. N1 : Classis NOS mode. O2 : 2X oversampling O4 : 4X oversampling O8 : 8X oversampling » - « Classis » is the page's spelling. Selecting N0 or N1 takes the interpolation filter out of the path, which is the precondition `correctable` requires.

_conditions_NON_CONCLUANTES_chez_Audio_g: No terms page found on audio-gd.com, so no prohibition could be checked - which is NOT the same as finding no prohibition. Measured 2026-11-25: the English navigation has seven items (Home, Products, Warranty, Shop, Contact Us, Shipment, Chinese) and no legal link; terms.htm, legal.htm, Copyright.htm and Privacy.htm all 404; Warranty-EN.htm was read in full and is a repair-and-shipping policy with no clause on content. There is no robots.txt (404). Every page carries the same footer, quoted as printed: « Copyright(C) 2004 www.audio-gd.com All Rights Reserved » - a bare reservation that states no prohibition on quoting. Same reading as Burson, Mytek and MHDT Labs: recorded because nothing forbidding was found, with the quality of the check recorded beside it.
_NOS_chez_Audio_gd_veut_dire_NON_SUR_ECH: 109 pages of this site were searched for « New Old Stock » and « N.O.S. »: ZERO hits. And one page defines the term outright: « In the 1970'S, the first generation of CDP were released , and they used an NOS design . "NOS" stands for "Non Oversampling". Using a NOS design, specs are ordinary because the limited signal bit depth affects THD and S/N. » The valve products are where the other meaning would have appeared and it does not - the Vacuum HE-1 MK3's pages contain no occurrence of NOS at all. So vocabulary/nos-means-two-things.json is settled for this maker in the direction the catalogue cares about, and the three models carrying NOS in their NAME - R-1 NOS, R-28 NOS, NOS-1704, plus the NOS 7 / 11 / 19 line - are non-oversampling designs, not valve-stock marketing.
_lechelle_de_VOLUME_nest_pas_le_converti: Audio-gd's volume controls are relay-switched resistor attenuators and the maker never calls them ladders: the wording is « a four channels digital control relays based volume control, through changing the tolerance 0.05% resistors to control the volume ». No page on this site conflates that with its R-2R converter, which is the trap that cost a withdrawn claim on another brand. ACSS is likewise not a digital input: it appears only under Output Level, as « 2+2MA (ACSS) », and as an ANALOGUE input on the amplifiers.
_les_chiffres_publies_sont_ceux_du_mode_: Every spec table on this site is headed « Specifications tested by OS8 mode » - the published S/N and THD figures are measured with 8x oversampling running, not in the non-oversampling mode this record's `correctable` depends on. The maker is explicit about the cost: on the R-1 NOS page, « if you want good specs, the NOS design definitely is not for you. » So the numbers and the mode that matters to an upsampling engine describe two different states of the same device, and no measurement is carried into this record.
_un_decodeur_DSD_SEPARE_du_convertisseur: « 8 group fully discrete R-2R PCM decoders » AND « 4 fully discrete real balanced DSD native decoders » - two converters in one box, one per format, both discrete. So `native_dsd` is true on a stronger basis than anywhere else in the catalogue: the maker is not claiming a transport, it is naming a separate hardware path that exists only to convert DSD. This is what `dsd_direct` was registered for and the field is still planned, so the fact lives in `chip` and in this gloss.
_un_optique_fantome_dans_le_tableau: The Input Sensitivity row lists « 19 dBm (Optical) » while the manual's input selector has exactly three inputs and none is optical, and the Support Sampling row gives no optical figure. So the sensitivity row is copied from a sibling model. inputs holds the three inputs the selector names and no optical entry - the absence is deliberate, and the stray row is quoted so a reader who finds it knows it was seen and rejected.
